title: Chapter 12: The Infantryman’s Creed
content: Chapter 12: The Infantryman’s Creed
I had successfully bought Louise and the others enough time to retreat, but as the decoy, my burden was reaching its limit.
“There are too many of them. Twenty? No, maybe thirty?”
Where on earth were they gathering from? Thirty Second Class Gijuu were chasing the Thunderbolt relentlessly.
Inside the cockpit of the fleeing Thunderbolt, I checked the instruments.
“Ammo count is fine. Energy is a bit worrying... but the propellant is clearly running low.”
I was flying at full throttle, but the jet engines’ propellant was almost gone. At this rate, I wouldn’t even be able to escape—I’d be surrounded and shot down.
“Ugh!”

A beam-like attack from a Gijuu grazed the Thunderbolt’s leg. Fortunately, the magic-generated force field reduced the damage, but because my magic power was low, the armor’s surface was heated and glowing red. It wasn’t melting yet, but taking concentrated fire was dangerous.
“So this is the protection of the force field... If only I’d had this back when I was infantry, how many lives could have been saved...”

My mind recalled the harsh memories of ground combat. Even Third Class Gijuu were a threat back then. If you were caught, survival was unlikely, and even grazing attacks often caused serious injuries. That’s why infantry were taught to evade thoroughly. We were trained to avoid enemy attacks rather than try to absorb them, focusing on dodging and striking back.
Against the overwhelming numbers of Gijuu, it was a strategy akin to throwing water on a burning stone—better than nothing, but barely enough.
Recalling my infantry tactics, I reached for a switch inside the cockpit—the magic power converter’s energy supply switch.
“That’s right. I am... a soldier!”

I toggled the switch that generated the force field protecting the armor, cutting off its magic supply. The magic power that had been used for defense now flowed to buoyancy and weapons. As the machine grew lighter, the Thunderbolt increased its speed.
“Yes, this is right. I might as well throw away defense from the start. That’s how I always fought on the ground.”

Though the environment on the ground was one where taking a hit meant certain death, the humanoid weapon I was piloting now was surprisingly good at dodging enemy attacks despite its heavy armor and armament. It avoided the Gijuu’ beam-like attacks with ease.
“Compared to running around on foot back then, this is nothing!”

Confirming that magic power was being supplied to the weapons, I raised the Gatling gun on my left arm and pulled the trigger. I sprayed bullets at the Gijuu chasing me, and compared to earlier, I was definitely dealing more damage. The bullets penetrated the force field generated by magic and reached the Gijuu’ outer shells, inflicting deeper wounds, as confirmed on the monitor.
That said, the damage was nowhere near as powerful as Louise’s. My magic power was insufficient from the start, and even cutting off the defense supply wasn’t enough. But it was enough for now.
“No problem. At this level, I can feel the effect more than I did in ground combat.”
It felt more effective now than when I used machine guns on the ground.
“With this much effect, I can fight properly.”

I stopped running as a decoy and, while keeping an eye on the propellant, continued attacking the Gijuu with the Gatling gun, eventually shooting one down. The Gijuu, unable to maintain its force field under constant fire, was riddled with bullets and fell into the sea.
Checking my ammo, I refined my fighting style.
“The ammo consumption is heavy for taking down one target. Relying solely on the Gatling gun is a bad move.”
I aimed the large rifle mounted on my right arm at the next Gijuu. It was a large rifle with a shortened barrel, which caused heavy recoil and made it unsuitable for sniping despite having a scope.
“If the power is high but accuracy is low—then I just need to get closer!”

When the Thunderbolt pulled the trigger, the cockpit shook violently. The powerful shot hit the Gijuu, but again, due to my lack of magic power, it wasn’t a killing blow. Still, it seemed to blast off the surface.
I fired a second and third shot at the Gijuu, which lost its balance in midair. After the third shot, it was destroyed and fell. I incorporated the large rifle into my fighting style.
“The missile is the problem...”

Thanks to the increased magic power supply to weapons, handling the missiles had changed. The large missile container mounted on my right shoulder had excellent penetration and explosive power. It was currently the Thunderbolt’s maximum firepower.

While suppressing the Gijuu with the Gatling gun, I found an easier target and locked on. A missile fired from the container flew faster than the smaller missiles and struck the Gijuu. It was pushed back slightly before a large explosion occurred.
The explosion produced flames and black smoke, and for a moment, I thought I saw something sparkling in the smoke—not just my imagination.
The Gijuu that fell from the smoke to the sea surface was dead.
Although my magic power was still insufficient, it seemed the missile’s firepower forcibly finished off the Second Class Gijuu after the force field was pierced by magic.
“Better not think about multi-locking.”

Only the large missile container had the power for a one-shot kill, but firing just once greatly depleted my magic power. It would be nice to use it repeatedly, but with my limited magic power, I couldn’t afford such luxuries.
“...Compared to ground combat, this is more than enough.”
In my mind, I already saw a chance of victory as I charged the Thunderbolt toward the Gijuu.
“Now it’s our turn to hunt!”
While Louise led the First Squad toward the makeshift base, fierce fighting was raging on the beach against Third Class Gijuu.
As I had expected, the infantry were taking heavy casualties on the ground.
“That was expected,” Louise said.
When she and three others arrived at the base, their homeroom teacher hurried over.
“Are all three of you safe?”
Louise saluted in her Battle Dress.
“Yes. But Ren-kun is still on the battlefield as a decoy.”
Louise’s bitter expression was met with relief from the teacher upon seeing the three safe students. However, it seemed he didn’t share a sense of camaraderie with Ren.
“The loss of an experimental machine is cheap if it means you candidates are protected.”

The Prometheus Project had an enormous budget, but when the teacher said “cheap loss,” it wasn’t just about money. He probably thought the project was unlikely to succeed and should be scrapped quickly. In other words, he valued the Valkyries above all.
Louise pleaded with the teacher.
“Please let me go rescue him!”
But the teacher’s response was cold.
“No.”
“Why!?”

“...Before you returned, we confirmed a mass outbreak of Second Class Gijuu. The Boots Cat Battalion is handling it, but they won’t make it in time. We’ve already committed all reserve forces here to protect this area.”
Told there were no forces left to mount a rescue, Louise hung her head.
“That’s...”
The teacher, thinking Louise was discouraged, placed a hand on her shoulder and spoke kindly.
“Thank you for the rescue. You should rest and wait.”
“...Understood.”
(Ren-kun... I wonder if you’re still alive? But there’s no way you could survive alone in that situation.)
Amid the swarm of Second Class Gijuu, I was learning aerial combat. It was very different from ground fighting, but in a way, the task was the same: defeat the Gijuu.
“You’re next.”

I chased a Gijuu, firing the Gatling gun to inflict wounds and cracks on its outer shell, then switched to the large rifle. Closing to a distance where I wouldn’t miss, I fired. The weakened part of the Gijuu couldn’t withstand the bullets and it died.
Suppress with the Gatling gun or create a weak point on the Gijuu’s shell. The finishing blow was a shot from the large rifle.
When the large rifle’s ammo ran out, I swapped magazines.
“Is that all the ammo?”

No spare magazines remained, and even the Gatling gun’s large drum magazine was nearly empty. Magic power supply was stable at thirty percent, but the machine’s energy and propellant were both unreliable.
“I regret wasting propellant at the start.”
Sweating inside the cockpit, I prioritized what I had to do. I dodged the Gijuu’ beam-like attacks and sharp claws with minimal movement while attacking.
After firing the last missile, I also jettisoned the large missile container. The Thunderbolt gradually became lighter, helping reduce propellant consumption.
I chipped away at the Gijuu with the Gatling gun and finished them off with the large rifle. In short, I just repeated this.
But the aerial battlefield and the unfamiliar Second Class Gijuu wore me down.
Before I knew it, I had jettisoned the Gatling gun and was left with only three shots in the large rifle.
“Only three rounds left... and the only weapon left is...”

Checking the machine’s weapons, the candidates displayed didn’t seem suitable for the current magic power output. It was inevitable, given the lack of other options, but I never thought I’d have to rely on this in such a situation.
A close-combat weapon that pierced Gijuu by supplying magic power to its blade—in other words, a dagger. Longer than a knife, I suppose? Dr. Smith said it was specially prepared for me.
I never imagined I’d actually have to use it.
Looking around, Gijuu still remained.
“No propellant left to outrun them... Let’s see if this works.”

I drew the dagger from behind my left knee with my left hand. When a Gijuu lunged with claws extended, I slashed it with the dagger on my left arm, then immediately aimed the large rifle. Pulling the trigger pierced the wound and killed the Gijuu.
“...Not bad.”

I quickly targeted another Gijuu, stabbed it with the dagger as it attacked, swiftly withdrew the blade, and kicked it away. After creating some distance, I pressed the large rifle’s muzzle to the wound and fired the finishing shot.
At that moment, I noticed something odd about the dagger’s blade length and the wound. The wound was clearly deeper and wider than the blade length.
“Is this also thanks to the magic force field? If so, there are plenty of ways to use this...”
I had assumed the humanoid weapon’s dagger would only scratch the surface of Second Class Gijuu, but if it could cut deeper, there were other uses.

When a Gijuu attacked from behind, I turned and fired the large rifle. As it was blown away, I closed the distance and tried to decapitate its head—the apparent weak spot—with the dagger in my left hand.
But it seemed I couldn’t cut as deeply as I thought. The Gijuu thrashed and fell into the sea, but was still alive.
“Is it the cutting technique? Or interference with the force field?”
I threw the large rifle aside and drew a dagger from behind my right knee as well. Dual-wielding felt like a long time ago.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/IpQa0Ap.jpeg
“Handling close-combat weapons in a humanoid machine requires consideration. Noticed variation in wound severity from the cut... probably due to...”
Muttering inside the cockpit, Gijuu gathered around. I dealt with them one by one.
The humanoid machine’s wrists had a wider range of motion than human wrists—they could rotate, so I didn’t have to hold the daggers backwards. That was an advantage.
I slashed at the approaching Gijuu, pondering the reason for the varying wound depths. I kept cutting until I figured out the cause, then tested it on the next target once one died.
“The close-combat weapons are more effective than firearms... Dr. Smith might be pleased, but Dr. Allison will probably be worried.”
When I decapitated the sixth Gijuu, I finally realized why the wounds varied in depth.
“Is it unstable magic power supply?”
Magic power supplied to the dagger generated a force field on the blade. However, the supply wasn’t constant, causing the wound depth to fluctuate.
I had found the cause, but immediate improvement was difficult. Still, it was reliable enough for now.
“—How ironic. Once you can handle force fields, the familiar weapon is more dependable than even the most powerful firearms!”
I stabbed a Gijuu’s head with the dagger. The vital point pierced, the Second Class Gijuu fell and sank into the sea without resistance.
From cutting, I roughly identified the Gijuu’ weak points.
With two daggers ready, I attacked the Gijuu.
“I know your weaknesses and attack methods... now all that’s left is to finish you off.”
Eliminating them with minimal movement, I cut off necks, struck vital points, and dodged attacks. I acted in ways Gijuu hated, clearing them out efficiently.
The Thunderbolt loomed over a Gijuu, plunging a dagger into it.
“One left.”
I withdrew the dagger as if kicking the Gijuu away, and the last one charged at me. It fired beam-like attacks rapidly, trying to slash the Thunderbolt with its sharp claws.
The Thunderbolt was nearing its limit. The machine groaned from repeated extreme maneuvers, and the daggers were in poor condition—blades chipped and cracked.
“...I’ll finish it as we pass by.”
I didn’t have enough propellant to get into a favorable position to strike. I waited, dagger ready, dodging the Gijuu’s attacks as it approached.
The beam-like attacks grazed the Thunderbolt, melting the armor. The thick armor was easily dissolved by the beams.
Still, the attacks only grazed, so the Gijuu closed in to finish me off.
It grabbed the Thunderbolt with sharp claws, easily piercing the thick armor and restraining me.
“I knew it would come to finish me off.”
I swung the dagger and cut off both its legs. The Gijuu writhed, but my left-hand dagger broke and became useless.
I stabbed the remaining dagger into its head and twisted—but the blade broke as well.
With that, the Thunderbolt lost all weapons and had no means to attack.
However, the last Gijuu sprayed bodily fluids from its wounds and slowly fell.
“Confirmed no other Gijuu nearby... enemy annihilated.”
Looking down at the Gijuu that fell into the sea, I steadied my ragged breathing.
I had exhausted a lot of stamina. My pilot suit was soaked with sweat and clung to my skin.
Alarms blared inside the cockpit—not only warning of low propellant but also severe damage to my overworked arms.
The manipulator joints screamed in protest; elbows and various parts were damaged.
They still moved, but repairing would take longer than replacing both arms.
“When I get back, Dr. Allison is going to scold me.”
I had thrown my weapons into the sea, where they sank. Recovery would be difficult, and besides my arms, other parts were damaged from the repeated extreme maneuvers.
I was barely able to move and gave up on returning on my own.
I sent a distress signal and prepared for the procedure to handle falling into the sea.
Maybe because I had released magic power for so long, I felt a unique nausea I had never experienced before.
But more than that, joy won out.
I let go of the control stick and stared at my right palm, clenching it tightly.
“I can fight. I’m still able to fight...”
The fact that I had won against Second Class Gijuu made me happier than anything.
The enemies I couldn’t beat as infantry, I had defeated now.
Suddenly, faces of my former squadmates flashed through my mind.
“...Everyone, I...”
At that moment, the radar caught a friendly unit’s response, and Louise’s face appeared on the monitor.
“I’ve come to pick you up, Ren-kun.”
Louise smiled, but I widened my eyes.
“Louise?”
The Louise on the screen was aiming a rifle.
“Au revoir, you damn Pseudo-beast impostor.”
A magic-charged beam fired from the large rifle in Louise’s Battle Dress, and the Thunderbolt’s monitor was flooded with white light.
